title: Dedupe Analyze Code Lens Per Line
description: The "Analyze" CodeLens in the VSCode extension renders multiple times above a single physical line when that line contains multiple top-level declarators (e.g. `export const a = ..., b = ..., c = ...;`). Every top-level definition should show one Analyze lens for all supported languages, but a single line must not produce multiple stacked lenses. Fix `collectNativeDefinitionCodeLenses` in `repo/vscode/extension.ts` to dedupe by line instead of by scope.
summary: Fixed `collectNativeDefinitionCodeLenses` in repo/vscode/extension.ts to dedupe Analyze CodeLenses per line: replaced scope-based dedup with a `linesSeen` Set keyed on `range.start.line`, so multi-declarator lines (e.g. `export const a = ..., b = ..., c = ...;`) produce exactly one Analyze lens. Extended the LSP symbol path with an always-on regex fallback merge so missing lines still get coverage. Updated the matching test helper `collectNativeDefinitionScopes` in extension.test.ts to mirror per-line dedup and extracted `collectNativeDefinitionFallbackEntries` returning {name, line}. Fixed two unrelated test-infra issues: `.vscode-test.mjs` used `workspacePath` (invalid option) instead of `workspaceFolder`, which caused `workspaceFolders` to be `undefined` in the test VS Code instance and made every native lens bail out at `getDocumentRelativePath`; and the CodeLens tests pointed at a non-existent `repo/go/events.go`, switched to `repo/go/main.go`. Verified: `npm test` shows the "Analyze CodeLens covers native definition scopes" test passing (771 native lenses produced for extension.ts). Remaining failures (URI parser, Filter Provider, Kit file detection, and entity-id coverage assertion in a fixture lacking entity IDs) are pre-existing and unrelated.
